review: 2:1 קָנָנוּ — 'He bought/acquired us'; the glossary fixes קָנָה for اشترى, and the perfect is used because the purchase is accomplished at the cross.
3:2 בַּנֶּהְדָּר הַהוּא — 'in that Glorious One', for فِي ذَاكَ الْمَجِيد; the adjective is substantivised with the article, as in Ps 8:2's בַּנֶּהְדָּר.
3:3–3:4 בְּאַהֲבָה נִקְשַׁר / לֹא בְמַסְמְרֵי בַּרְזֶל — 'bound by love, not by iron nails'; the antithesis is the whole point of the stanza and is kept word for word.
4:4 מַפְגִּיעַ — the glossary word for intercession (Isa 53:12), used again here as in hymn 5.
6:2 כָּל־עוֹד אַתָּה שָׁם — 'while You are there', for طَالَمَا أَنْتَ هُنَاك; the Arabic طَالَمَا is 'as long as', and the Hebrew clause mirrors it.
6:3 נְיַחֵל לַבּוֹאֶךָ — 'we wait for Your coming'; the piel of יחל is the biblical verb of waiting in hope (Ps 42:6).
